cards.summary: 2.10.7 HA add-on, Sonos Port 'Office' (line-out Variable). cards.fix: server#7132 (draft): the flow route passes on whatever ffmpeg has encoded (read-any) when ICY is off, instead of waiting for a full second of encoded audio (~197 KB for FLAC). Hermetic pytest repro: exact chunk size gives the first byte after 17.3 s on 20 s of silence, read-any under 3 s. ICY is off by default, so HEOS takes this path. cards.area: frontend / mediaSession play handlers (PlayerBrowserMediaControls.vue, SendspinPlayer.vue) + server players/controller.py _handle_cmd_pause
cards.summary: 2.11.0b5 Docker. Opening the web UI makes a 2-HomePod AirPlay sync group play a few seconds of the radio station left in its stopped queue. It also started on its own at 05:18 with nobody at the UI. Verbose webserver log: players/cmd/play and players/cmd/pause for the syncgroup 1 ms apart, then two more pauses, all while the queue is still IDLE, so every pause is dropped and the group starts. Report written with Claude, diagnostics attached (uptime 18 min, doesn't cover either event).
cards.checked: Code read on frontend origin/main and server origin/dev, no repro. The frontend only sends play/pause from the mediaSession action handlers (PlayerBrowserMediaControls.vue:149-160, SendspinPlayer.vue:455-470) and the companion tray (companion.ts:296-300). Both browser handlers delay pause by 250 ms, so a play and pause 1 ms apart is not one click: it fits a pause action ~250 ms before a play action, i.e. the OS or browser firing media keys (tab grabbing Now Playing, headphones connecting, Mac waking). Nothing in the page-load path calls play itself, the silent <audio> element play() never reaches the server. The 05:18 start without anyone opening the UI points the same way: an MA tab or app left open somewhere. Server side, _handle_cmd_pause returns early when the player is IDLE (controller.py:5101), so a pause that lands while a play is still starting the group is lost. The Received: log line has no client id, so the log can't say which tab or device sent it. 10-21 (frontend origin/main = b5's 2.17.341 on these paths): in 'Built-in web player only' mode PlayerBrowserMediaControls.vue is never mounted (App.vue:35, :137-144) and SendspinPlayer.vue's handlers (455-470) target the web player only (getTargetPlayerId :442); keyboard and player buttons send play_pause, visibility/focus handlers send no commands, the companion tray needs Tauri. cards.summary: Cause found by reading the code; not reproduced, because that needs a Navidrome with two users. Both Subsonic instances map to the same library artist. The opensubsonic parser stamps the artist cover_art thumb with provider=<instance id> and remotely_accessible=False. The frontend's imageIsUsable (src/helpers/utils.ts:364) only accepts a non-remote image if api.getProvider(img.provider) is available, and api.providers only holds the viewer's own visible sources. So maA gets the initials fallback for an image stamped with maB's instance. The flip: opening an artist runs music/refresh_item with overwrite=True, which replaces the stored images with the refreshing user's instance-stamped ones, so the other user loses them. Likely cause: metadata_for_update (controllers/music/helpers.py:136) returns the update as is on an overwrite, images included. Opening an artist runs refresh_item with overwrite=True from the viewer's own source, so the other account's images are dropped from the stored row and server#6708 has nothing usable left to pick for that user.

cards.title: Sonos volume still delayed and stepped when bridged via AirPlay into a group with a Sendspin player (2.10.5, follow-up to #6110)
cards.area: server / providers/sonos + airplay (Sendspin to AirPlay bridge)
cards.summary: 2.10.5 HA add-on. A Sonos Move 2 (native SONOS preferred, AirPlay second) grouped with a Sendspin player (Echo Show 5, TECHO5 firmware) plays over the Sendspin to AirPlay bridge. Volume changes for it land 20-65 s late, one partial step per cycle, and keep stepping through old slider values after the user stopped. PTP timing shortens the cycle to ~20-26 s, buffer size and "ignore volume reports" change nothing. Same symptom as the closed support#6110 (Aug), which the reporter of that one thought 2.10.0 fixed.
cards.checked: Code read on origin/dev 61842140c and 2.10.5 (identical on this path), plus cliairplay v0.5.5 and aiosonos 0.1.13. With the Sonos rendering over AirPlay, volume_control still resolves to NATIVE, so MA sends the user's volume through aiosonos setVolume and never through AirPlay. No MA-side queue fits a ~65 s cadence: the per-player VOLUME lock gives up after 30 s, the AirPlay VOLUME pipe write is non-blocking, cliairplay runs each VOLUME as one SET_PARAMETER with a 2 s budget, and nothing in airplay/sonos/sendspin/players has a 60-70 s timer. The diagnostics show the bridge restarting often, DACP server running, and one 5 s SET_PARAMETER timeout at 13:42, but no volume lines (not debug). Likely (about 35%) the Sonos itself serializes native volume while it's in an AirPlay 2 session with DACP, the same device behaviour as #6110. The timing-mode effect fits a device-side cause better than an MA one. Staying on AirPlay after the Sendspin player leaves is by design on 2.10.5. server#6675 (in 2.11.0b4) moves the group back to native sync on the next start. Not reproducible here: Sonos is off-limits at night and the cadence needs real hardware. 10-14: Opus subagent on mawi13's 10-13 test (2.10.6, Move 2 on 27.1). MA never sent a volume to Küche: every cmd_volume_set is for Echo Show 5 (its own Sendspin role, controller.py:4199-4208), Küche (AirPlay) group_volume lines are just the max-of-members display (player.py:1604-1629), and every Küche volume_level change starts as a device report (mirror triplets 19:00:40-19:07:47). mawi13's own native 25 % test via HA was held until the AirPlay session ended, so the 65 s grid is the Sonos holding native-API volume during AirPlay. MA's part: __control_for_output returns NATIVE whenever the parent supports VOLUME_SET (player.py:2468), and the AirPlay output doesn't own volume for a Sonos-linked output (airplay/player.py:935-948), so MA's own changes take the held native path too. No 60/65 s timer in MA. Nothing on dev. Their log excerpt was filtered (no DACP lines). 10-21 investigation session (your approval to post): HA's Sonos integration isn't the cause of the delay; the speaker held both MA's aiosonos change and the HA SoCo 25 % set. The 10-07 diagnostics show hass player_controls 0, so no HA entity was a volume control. The sender of Küche's 10-13 steps is unknown: an HA dashboard/automation on the HA Sonos entity, or the Sendspin bridge role path (airplay/sendspin_bridge.py _on_volume_change > AirPlayPlayer.volume_set sends VOLUME= without an owns_volume check). A solo AirPlay test removes the bridge.

cards.title: Sendspin→AirPlay bridge drops 1.7-3.3 s at stream start, and schedules each player at a different lead — a fixed, audible offset between RAOP players in one sync group
cards.summary: The dropped intro is real: on a realtime source (Spotify via soloist, YouTube Music, radio) Sendspin ignores the bridge's 4500 ms cold-start lead and schedules only min_buffer_ms (1000 ms) ahead, while the bridge can never anchor sooner than connect time + 2500 ms, so ~1.7-2.2 s is always cut on a cold start. The "per-player lead = audible offset" claim is disproved by the reporter's own log: the start_unix_ms gap (188 ms) equals the content-shift gap (2188-2000), so both players map the same sample to the same instant. The constant ~199 ms echo is device output latency, which is what sync_adjust is for. Code is identical between 2.10.3 and origin/dev.
cards.checked:
live_verdict: BLOCKED
lane: live
repro_cmd: worktree triage-6419 (origin/dev fd034e289) + cliairplay v0.5.4 in providers/airplay/bin; `ma-live.sh prepare`, set players.9056826F550E.values.preferred_output_protocol=spb_9056826f550e and players.ap9056826f550e.values.stored_volume=0 in the copy, `ma-live.sh start`, then `triage_logs/2026-09-27/repro/6419.sh <uri> 8` (not run: the pre-play volume guard failed)
evidence: No playback started. The caller's guard (volume 0 on the NAD AirPlay player and parent, abort if any NAD player reads above 5) can't be met. `players/cmd/volume_set` on ap9056826f550e/spb_9056826f550e is auto-resolved to the parent ("Auto-resolved protocol player spb_9056826f550e to linked parent 9056826F550E"), so over the API only the parent goes to 0. With the default config ap/spb read 400 (raw FALLBACK_VOLUME 20 under max_volume=5). With stored_volume=0 seeded, ap reads 0 but spb reads 500. Cause: `sendspin_bridge.py:438` `initial_volume=self.airplay_player.volume_level or 25`, where a 0 is falsy, so the bridge role starts at raw 25. `_enforce_volume_limits` then tries `_handle_cmd_volume_set(spb, 100)` (seen at registration, where it failed with "Player spb_9056826f550e is not available"). On a later state update while streaming, that clamp goes spb.volume_set(5) -> role -> `airplay_player.volume_set(5)` -> `VOLUME=5` to the NAD, even though BluOS owns its volume (this path skips the `owns_volume` gate). Under max_volume=5 every protocol-player reading is scaled x20, so any non-zero device volume reads >= 20. The literal "nothing above 5" guard can only hold at device volume 0.
unblock options (need a human decision): (a) guard on device scale instead (parent logical <= 5, ap/spb raw <= 5, no `VOLUME=` > 5 in run.log). The known worst case is a clamp push of VOLUME=5. (b) Seed ap stored_volume=1 and drop max_volume from only the two protocol players, so spb/ap read 1 and nothing gets clamped. The parent keeps max_volume=5 and owns the volume.
side note (harness): the watchdog clamped WiiM Mini (idle) from volume 100 to 5 nine times right after start. It then read 0. Nothing played.

cards.title: HEOS Integration plays announcements N times
cards.area: server / heos (player provider) + streams announcement URL
cards.summary: Repeated announcements on a HEOS speaker (Denon Home 150) play 1x, 2x, 3x. HEOS `browse/play_stream` appends to the device queue and starts playback at qid 1, MA's queue cleanup always keeps the "current" entry (so one stale MA entry survives every session) and the queue-connection `get_queue` is answered ~20s late, so cleanup never catches up. Every stale entry points at the same per-player `/announcement/{player_id}.mp3` URL, which serves the new announcement, so the device plays it once per queue entry; virtual repro goes red with `[1, 2, 3]`.
cards.fix: None. The fix means bringing back HEOS queue clearing (reworked before in #3932) and depends on real-device timing, or a controller-wide announcement URL change. This needs a decision with Tommatheussen. The plan is above.
cards.checked: A/B: A=n/a B=n/a A2=n/a
cards.plan:
Checked on origin/dev 3e1d945d0. `play_media` only calls `play_url` (`browse/play_stream`, which appends). `_cleanup_heos_queue` keeps `now_playing.queue_id` and runs only while `PLAYING`. The announcement URL is stable per player (`/announcement/{player_id}.{fmt}`). So the cause holds.

Why this isn't implemented unattended:
- Option 1 (keep the max qid and `player_play_queue` to it) does not fix the captured timeline on its own. `get_queue` on the queue connection answered after ~20s, which is after the next announcement's `play_stream`, so the "newest" qid is already stale when cleanup runs. A jump mid-announcement could also cut or restart the clip. Whether that is audible can only be checked on a real HEOS device.
- Option 2 (non-blocking `player_clear_queue` on the queue connection once MA playback reaches STOP) is the likely core fix. But it brings back queue clearing, which Tommatheussen reworked several times (ghost items, then #3932 because it blocked volume commands). Whether a clear on the secondary connection is fast enough, and doesn't race the next `play_stream`, is device behaviour we can't check here.
- Option 3 (a nonce per announcement in the URL, 404 on mismatch) is a controller change that affects every player provider. A maintainer should decide that.

Proposed direction, to agree with Tommatheussen:
1. HEOS: on transition to STOP/idle while `_ma_controls_playback`, schedule `player_clear_queue` on `_heos_queue` (fire-and-forget, logged on HeosError). Cancel it if a new `play_media` starts first.
2. HEOS: in `play_media`, if a clear is still in flight, await it (with a short timeout) before `play_url`, so the new stream lands on an empty queue at qid 1.
3. Keep `_cleanup_heos_queue` for multi-item flow sessions. Optionally switch it to keep the max qid.
4. Optional/separate: make announcement URLs unique per announcement (controller side), so stale queue entries on any player 404 instead of replaying the new clip.
Regression test: extend `tests/providers/heos/test_repro_6400.py` (fake device with delayed `get_queue`) to assert `[1, 1, 1]`.
notes: 10-19 07:38 run: Dragon-Creature (10-18 02:31 UTC): clearing the queue in Music Assistant didn't help, clearing the HEOS queue on the speaker itself did. That matches the root cause (stale entries in the HEOS device queue that MA never clears, all pointing at the same announcement URL) and supports option 2 (clear the HEOS queue when MA playback stops). Nothing else new.
10-26 07:30 run: Tommatheussen answered the ping with an approach (clear queue, announce, restore). Waiting on him; answer draft dropped.
cards.action: Tommatheussen (10-23) proposes: clear the HEOS queue before an announcement, no repeat, restore after. His to build.

cards.title: [Party Plugin] Party mode guest access fails over QR code if blocked by IPv6 stateful firewall
cards.area: server / webserver remote_access (WebRTC gateway) + party plugin
cards.summary: Party guests on dual-stack networks time out ("Timeout waiting for server info") while IPv4-only guests connect; reporter's router blocks inbound IPv6. The join URL always goes through WebRTC via app.music-assistant.io when remote access is on, and in "basic" mode MA only offers public STUN (no TURN), so a peer pair where both hole-punch paths fail cannot connect. The reporter says he has HA Cloud, which would add TURN, but diagnostics show the hass provider failed at startup (502 from supervisor websocket). That can leave remote access in basic mode, and it matches his report that `iceTransportPolicy: relay` still failed. Marvin asked today (2026-09-27) whether Settings > Remote access shows optimized mode; that answer is still outstanding. Update 10-01 22:33 UTC: the reporter confirms Optimized Mode is active. A code read (origin/dev) finds no guest-specific path: the QR/join-code guest uses the same WebRTCTransport and signaling route as a normal user and gets the same iceServers list, and nothing in the gateway filters IPv6. The gateway drops turn:?transport=tcp and turns: URLs (libjuice is UDP-only), so a guest network that blocks UDP 3478 can't relay. Remaining suspects: UDP/TURN blocked on the guest side, the server's own TURN allocation failing, or a v6 candidate pair stalling behind the inbound-IPv6 block.

cards.title: Universal Player config deleted at startup by a stale native link, recreated with a new id
cards.summary: After upgrading 2.10.2 to 2.10.6, a Juke Audio / Volumio AirPlay player wrapped in a Universal Player came back with a new player_id (upfc94fc52 became up56917d04). At startup MA declined to restore the UP because its AirPlay protocol was recorded as linked to a native player, deleted the UP config, and when no native showed up it wrapped the same AirPlay protocol in a new UP. No diagnostics yet.
cards.checked: Opus subagent, code read on origin/dev (87a250a1e5), same in 2.10.2 and 2.10.6. discover_players (universal_player/provider.py:65-89) calls _restore_player (:308) per stored UP. The native_claims loop (:349-367) treats any non-UP config whose stored linked_protocol_ids holds the UP's AirPlay id as the rightful owner, guarded only by _owns_domain_of_protocols (:511, #6610). It reparents the protocol to that native (:532) and deletes the UP config (:389-401) before the native registers. At runtime _try_link_protocol_to_native (protocol_linking.py:161-198) waits 45 s for the cached parent (:448), _delayed_protocol_evaluation (:466-530) creates a UP, and _resolve_stored_universal_player (:621) finds no config via the rewritten protocol_parent_id, so mint_player_id() (:239) makes the new id. Root cause of the stale claim: _save_linked_protocol_ids (:1522-1540) only ever adds ids, so a native that once linked the AirPlay protocol keeps claiming it. #6610 (2.10.5) only covers a stale native that owns its own AirPlay protocol. The existing test test_restore_native_claims_carries_config_and_deletes_wrapper (test_protocol_linking.py:11173) asserts today's deletion with this exact config shape. Likely stale native: an MPD or HA player for the Volumio box (guess). No open PR.
cards.plan: Fix doesn't depend on diagnostics. Lean shape agreed in chat; fix also covers home-assistant/core#187029 (mint on fallback).

cards.title: Eversolo Squeeze Connect players reconnect to slimproto every ~130 s
cards.summary: Eversolo T8 and DMP-A6 using built-in Squeeze Connect drop and reconnect to MA's slimproto server about every 130 seconds, which interrupts playback. It still happens on 2.10.7 (Docker on a Pi 5, host networking). LMS is stable with the same devices. The reporter's captures show RSTs from the Eversolo side and CLOSE-WAIT sockets piling up on the MA side. Update 10-21: firmware 1.6.15 on both; idle tests on 2.10.7 show the cycle with both players, T8 alone (130.28 s) and DMP-A6 alone (127.28 s). Offers a tcpdump on port 3483.
cards.checked: Attached log: the DMP-A6 cycles 'Player unavailable' then 'connected' every 129-131 s from 08:30 on. It starts right after the provider loads and while nothing plays, so it is not playback related. The T8 does not cycle in this log. aioslimproto (3.2.3 on stable, 3.3.0 on dev) sends strm 't' every 5 s (client.py _send_heartbeat, HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL=5 in const.py). After each heartbeat it calls _render_display, which sends display/brightness frames unless the player reported a 0x0 display. The socket reader drops the client after 10 s of silence (client.py _socket_reader, timeout HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL*2). Nothing in the code gives a 130 s period, and the log is INFO only, so we can't see which side closes or why. One guess, not verified: the display frames sent every 5 s to a squeezeplay-type device with no display. The CLOSE-WAIT buildup points to a possible missed close in aioslimproto disconnect(), but I could not tie it to the cycle. 10-21: the three Verbose logs hold no aioslimproto lines at all. Log-level-only config changes skip the provider reload (models/provider.py:136), and the Squeezelite provider sets the aioslimproto logger level only in handle_async_init (squeezelite/provider.py:69-73), so it stayed at WARNING. All three logs come from the same 05:24 boot with Verbose set at 05:37. Same code on stable. Reconnect lands 140-170 ms after 'unavailable' each time, so the device redials immediately; which side closes is still unknown. 10-21 14:30: Vivi92821's 11:32 capture: the T8 closes first (RST, then FIN every ~127 s) and reconnects ~130 ms later; MA's own FIN on the old socket lands ~52 s late. The Verbose log and diagnostics it mentions are not attached, only a findings txt. In squeezeplay a ~130 ms reconnect comes from LocalPlayer connectToServer/connectIp (Comet serverstatus on 9000, a serv frame or discovery, DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT 120 s), not the slimproto read timeout (35 s, random 1-5 s backoff); confidence ~35%, Eversolo firmware is closed. Separate real bug: aioslimproto _socket_reader sets _connected False (client.py:652 in 3.2.3, :665 in 3.3.0) and then calls disconnect(), which returns early (:124), so write_eof/close never run and the socket sits in CLOSE-WAIT until GC. 10-21 15:30 (Verbose log + PCAP, TCP 3483 only): per session MA sends vers, setd, aude, audg, grfb, grfe; the T8 only SETD, then strm t every 5 s answered within ~2 ms; nothing left unanswered. Each slimproto session lasts 127.13 s; every 127.04 s the T8 starts a brand-new CometD /meta/handshake on port 9000 and drops slimproto 3.25-3.97 s later, no /meta/reconnect. So a client-side ~127 s timer above slimproto (~85%); what arms it (UDP discovery, Comet content, Eversolo watchdog) ~35%. If MA can fix it, likely in aioslimproto cli.py (cometd) or discovery.py. The 52 s late FIN is the separate disconnect() early-return bug.
cards.plan: Compare an idle T8 capture against LMS with one against MA (host filter, incl. UDP discovery). Separately: fix the aioslimproto CLOSE-WAIT bug (see follow-ups).

cards.title: DLNA: LUMIN-based renderers (TEAC NR-7CD) stay silent because MA ignores Range
cards.summary: A TEAC NR-7CD with a LUMIN network module accepts MA's DLNA stream and reports PLAYING but stays silent. The renderer reads with Range requests (bytes=0-, 12-, 16384-, ...). MA answers each one with 200 OK from byte 0 and 'Accept-Ranges: none', so the decoder gets data at the wrong offset. The reporter showed that the same bytes play fine from a server that supports Range, and has a working proxy workaround. Version 2.10.6, HA add-on.
cards.checked: DEFAULT_STREAM_HEADERS sets 'Accept-Ranges: none' (constants.py:905-913). It is used by every stream endpoint in controllers/streams/controller.py (182, 861, 1018, 1477, 1661-1685), and there is no Range handling anywhere in the streams controller. Each GET on /single/ starts a fresh pipeline from 0. Ignoring Range and sending 200 is valid HTTP, so the renderer is out of spec, but the behaviour is as described. No open server PR or other support issue on this. Supporting it means keeping a per-session head buffer and answering 206 for offsets inside it, which is a design change to live streams, not a small fix.
cards.plan: If variant 1 fails and 2 or 3 plays: fix the DIDL protocolInfo to DLNA.ORG_OP=00 (match the response header). If all three fail: close as a firmware limitation (needs a range-capable server), proxy as the workaround. Full Range support is off the table (live encode).

cards.summary: After switching from filesystem to Emby (DB reset, same FLAC files), migrating an old MA playlist to MA picks Qobuz tracks or skips tracks instead of using the Emby copies; Exact/Same recording/Best effort give different results. 2.11.0b5, Docker.

Resume position is already carried over (resume_pos, dev:1324, PR #4115), so 0:00 is a side effect of the failed start. ~/.musicassistant has no Tidal provider, although the triage spec says YT Music, Apple Music, Spotify and Tidal are configured there (found 10-16 via #6759). Add a Tidal account or fix the spec.
Local files logs 'Error processing <file> - ' with an empty message when the exception has no text (AssertionError in #6815). Logging the exception type would make these diagnosable at INFO level.

server#6706 (Cast artwork in a Universal Group, draft) lost its issue: #6102 was auto-closed. voc0der replied after the close (10-20 09:55 UTC) that they won't test without a docker image. Keep it as a standalone fix or close it.
#6668 (closed by you 10-20 as a tagging issue): the get_album_dir exact-tier bug for self-titled album folders still has a clean unit repro and no fix. Worth a small PR if you want it.
HA core music_assistant handle_player_config_updated defaults a missing expose_player_to_ha to True (#6822). Small HA core PR: fall back to the client player's expose_to_ha.

Squeezelite: setting the provider log level to Verbose at runtime never reaches the aioslimproto logger (set only in handle_async_init, log-level changes skip the reload). Override update_config to re-apply the level. Found on #6800, same on stable.

AirPlay: _adopt_device_volume (airplay/player.py:828-839, 1031-1044) and the Sendspin bridge volume path send VOLUME= without an owns_volume check; a candidate MA-side cause for Sonos volume snapping back during AirPlay (#6838, #6664).

aioslimproto: disconnect() returns early after _socket_reader sets _connected False (client.py:652/658 in 3.2.3, :665/671 in 3.3.0), so the old socket is never closed and sits in CLOSE-WAIT (#6800). One-line fix in aioslimproto; reproducible with plain squeezelite (kill the client, `ss -tan state close-wait '( sport = :3483 )'`).
issue-triage release_table: for an unreleased patch milestone (2.10.8) check the backport branch (backport/2.10.8), not origin/stable; 'on stable' reads as 0 until the release.

Frontend: the shuffle-off icon (two straight arrows, ShuffleBtn.vue IconArrowsRight) doesn't read as shuffle; #6757's reporter toggled Repeat thinking it was Shuffle. Small UX chip: use a crossed-arrows icon in both states, colour for on.

server: _player_options (helpers/config_entries.py:119-128) offers live private web players in plugin connected-players pickers. Agreed fix from the #6773 discussion: skip players that are both private and hide_in_ui, mirroring the frontend's groupMemberPickerVisible. Independent of #6773's answer.

Core: queue play actions hold the player's playback lock through play_index's skip loop (15 s BUFFER_READY_TIMEOUT per unplayable item), so a cmd_stop waits up to 30 s (#6840). Consider letting a stop/handoff preempt the skip loop.
